Lie theory OurBigBook.com
An affine algebraic group is an affine variety G whose multiplication and inversion are regular maps. Equivalently, its coordinate ring k[G] is a commutative Hopf algebra, with comultiplication induced by multiplication in G.

Adjoint Chevalley group

Words: 130 Articles: 1
Linear algebraic group OurBigBook.com
Fix a Chevalley basis and its integral lattice. The adjoint Chevalley group over a field is generated by the root operators obtained from the integral divided-power polynomials xα​(t)=∑j​tj(adeα​)j/j! on that lattice. The coefficients are first computed over the integers and then reduced to the field; factorials need not be invertible there. This is the adjoint construction; other weight lattices give other isogeny forms of groups of Lie type.

x+​(t)ex−​(s)f​=e,=f,​x+​(t)hx−​(s)h​=h−2te,=h+2sf,​x+​(t)fx−​(s)e​=f+th−t2e,=e−sh−s2f.​
(1)
These are conjugation by the upper and lower elementary matrices of the special linear group. Those matrices generate SL2​(K), and a matrix commuting with both E12​ and E21​ is scalar. Thus the kernel is precisely {aI:a2=1} over every field, even in characteristic two, and the image is the displayed quotient.

An algebraic one-parameter subgroup is a regular group homomorphism from the multiplicative algebraic group. In SLn​, a change of basis makes it t↦diag(ta1​,…,tan​) for integers with sum zero. This is the algebraic multiplicative notion, distinct from an additive real-parameter subgroup of a Lie group.

Words: 167 Articles: 1
Linear algebraic group OurBigBook.com
For every finite-dimensional rational representation V and every nonzero v∈VG, a geometrically reductive algebraic group admits a homogeneous invariant polynomial F∈k[V]G of positive degree with F(v)=0. A linearly reductive group can take degree one. In positive characteristic, higher degree is essential: a power pr can separate a fixed vector even when an invariant linear functional cannot.

Determinant separation for positive-characteristic SL2 (q=pr,det:End(Symq−1k2)→k)

Words: 109
Geometrically reductive algebraic group OurBigBook.com
Choose a torus-invariant functional nonzero on a fixed vector, and map the representation to right-torus-invariant matrix coefficients on SL2​. These functions lie in a finite filtration by polynomials of bidegree (n,n) in the two matrix columns. For n=q−1, all binomial coefficients are nonzero in characteristic p, so the invariant tensor given by the determinant to power n induces an invertible map from the symmetric power's dual to itself. The filtration piece becomes its endomorphism space, with the constant function corresponding to the identity. The endomorphism determinant is an invariant degree-q polynomial equal to one there; composing it with the original representation map proves geometric reductivity.

Linearly reductive algebraic group

Words: 51
Linear algebraic group OurBigBook.com
An affine algebraic group is linearly reductive when every finite-dimensional rational representation is completely reducible. Equivalently its invariants functor is exact. Over a field of characteristic zero, reductive algebraic groups are linearly reductive; in positive characteristic this stronger property fails for many reductive groups. An algebraic torus is linearly reductive in every characteristic because its rational representations decompose into character spaces.

Linear algebraic group OurBigBook.com
A rational structure over Fq​ is a model over that finite field together with its identification after extension to Fq​. It determines a Frobenius endomorphism of an algebraic group, whose fixed points are the rational points. Conjugating a standard Frobenius by an algebraic group automorphism transports the rational structure, even if the automorphism is not itself rational for the original structure.

For an algebraic group defined over Fq​, its Frobenius morphism acts as entrywise qth powers in a standard matrix realization. Its differential is zero, and its fixed-point group is finite. A conjugate F′=φFφ−1 defines an isomorphic rational structure. This group morphism must be distinguished from a field Frobenius endomorphism alone and from the convention called geometric Frobenius in Galois theory, which is inverse to the arithmetic generator on field points.

Since dF=0, every orbit map has surjective differential, so each orbit is open; connectedness leaves only one orbit. The same differential calculation makes the Lang map étale, with finite fibres equal to left cosets of GF.

A rational representation is a group homomorphism whose matrix coefficients are regular functions on the affine algebraic group. For the general linear group, those functions are polynomials in matrix entries and the inverse determinant. The word rational does not permit poles at points of the group.

A vector is unstable if zero lies in the Zariski closure of its orbit. For complex SLn​, this is equivalent to an algebraic one-parameter subgroup taking it to zero as t→0. In the subgroup's weight decomposition, exactly the positive-weight components can occur in such a vector.

Words: 131 Articles: 1

For complex SLn​, choose a sequence taking an unstable vector to zero and apply singular value decomposition to each group element. Compactness gives a limiting right-unitary factor. Every nonzero torus-weight component of the transformed vector forces a strict linear inequality on the diagonal exponents. A rational solution of these finitely many strict inequalities scales to integral exponents with sum zero, producing an algebraic one-parameter subgroup that takes the vector to zero. The converse follows immediately from the subgroup limit.

For diag(t,t−1), the monomial xd−iyi has weight d−2i. Positive weights force divisibility by x⌊d/2⌋+1. Conjugating the subgroup replaces x by any nonzero linear factor. Thus a nonzero binary form is unstable exactly when a projective root has multiplicity greater than half its degree. Equality gives zero weight and does not imply instability.

Rational representation OurBigBook.com
For finite-dimensional rational representations of complex GLm​ or SLm​, average a Hermitian inner product over the compact group U(m) or SU(m) using normalized Haar measure. Orthogonal complements become invariant under the compact group and its complexified Lie algebra. The latter generates the complex group, giving invariant complements and hence complete reducibility. This conclusion does not hold for arbitrary affine algebraic groups, such as the additive group.

A proper closed normal subgroup likewise has zero-dimensional Lie algebra, hence is finite; connectedness of G makes conjugation on that finite subgroup trivial, so the subgroup is central. A Lie group homomorphism onto a nontrivial connected target with surjective differential consequently has finite central group kernel. The qualifications “proper” and “nontrivial” are essential.

Lie product formula in a Lie group (exp(t(X+Y))=limm→∞​(exp(tX/m)exp(tY/m))m)

Words: 51
Exponential map of a Lie group OurBigBook.com
The Lie product formula extends from matrices to any finite-dimensional Lie group. In a local exponential chart, smooth multiplication and its differential give log(exp(sX)exp(sY))=s(X+Y)+O(s2). Taking s=t/m and using the one-parameter subgroup identity shows that the mth power is exp(t(X+Y)+O(m−1)), proving the displayed limit. This proof needs only the first-order expansion, rather than convergence of the full Baker--Campbell--Hausdorff formula.

Naturality of the Lie group exponential (F(expG​v)=expH​(De​Fv))

Words: 61
Exponential map of a Lie group OurBigBook.com
For a Lie group homomorphism F, the image of the integral curve through the identity of a left-invariant vector field is the integral curve of the field induced by its differential. Uniqueness of integral curves of a vector field identifies the curves for all times. Evaluating at time one gives the formula. Completeness of invariant fields follows from left translation and repetition of a local integral curve, independently of a matrix-series formula.

Local exponential chart (log:exp(U)⟶U⊆g)

Words: 44
Exponential map of a Lie group OurBigBook.com
Since the differential of the Exponential map of a Lie group at zero is the identity, the inverse function theorem makes it a diffeomorphism on a sufficiently small neighborhood of zero. Its local inverse is a logarithm near the group identity. It need not extend to a global logarithm, even for the real general linear group.

Lie group OurBigBook.com
The Cayley transform is a rational local parametrization of a matrix Lie group from its Lie algebra wherever I−X is invertible. Unlike the exponential map, its image can meet nonidentity components.

A Coxeter group is a group with a presentation
W=⟨xi​ (i∈I):(xi​xj​)mij​=1⟩,
(13)
where mii​=1 and mij​=mji​∈{2,3,…,∞} for i=j. The pair consisting of W and its distinguished generating reflections is a Coxeter system.

A Coxeter system (W,I,M) records a Coxeter group W, its set I of simple generators, and its Coxeter matrix M=(mij​).

The Coxeter matrix of a Coxeter system is the symmetric matrix whose entry mij​ is the order of xi​xj​.
Coxeter graph
Words: 189 Articles: 3
Coxeter matrix OurBigBook.com
The Coxeter graph has vertex set I, joins i and j when mij​≥3, and labels the edge by mij​ when mij​>3. A Coxeter system is irreducible exactly when this graph is connected.
Admissible crystallographic Coxeter graph (Gii​=1,Gij​=−nij​​/2)
Words: 107
Coxeter graph OurBigBook.com
In the crystallographic convention, a Coxeter graph is admissible when it is realized by linearly independent unit vectors vi​ in a Euclidean space, with nonpositive mutual inner products and 4(vi​,vj​)2=nij​∈{0,1,2,3} for distinct vertices. The number nij​ records a single, double or triple connection; equivalently, the displayed Gram matrix is positive-definite. In edge-label notation the nonzero connections have labels 3,4,6. Forgetting multiplicity, the underlying graph is a forest: for any cycle of k≥3 distinct vertices, the sum of the corresponding unit vectors would have squared norm at most k−k=0, contradicting their linear independence. Multiple lines on one connection are labels and are not length-two cycles. This is the convention of Wehler's Lie algebra notes, section 6.3.
Irreducible Coxeter system
Words: 24
Coxeter graph OurBigBook.com
An irreducible Coxeter system is one whose Coxeter graph is connected. The connected components of a Coxeter graph give the direct-product decomposition of its Coxeter group.
Type E(p,q,k) Coxeter graph (E(p,q,k))
Words: 25
Coxeter graph OurBigBook.com
The type E(p,q,k) graph is a simply-laced tree with one trivalent vertex and arms containing p, q, and k vertices beyond that vertex.

Coxeter system OurBigBook.com
A reduced expression in a Coxeter group has the least possible Coxeter length among expressions in the generators of its Coxeter system.
A reduced expression for w∈W is a product of the fewest possible simple generators representing w. The number of factors is its Coxeter length ℓ(w).
Deletion condition for involutory generators
Words: 71 Articles: 1
Reduced expression in a Coxeter group OurBigBook.com
For a group generated by involutions, the deletion condition says that every nonreduced word can be shortened without changing its value by deleting two of its letters.
Folding-grid proof of the deletion condition
Words: 44
Deletion condition for involutory generators OurBigBook.com
Arrange the lengths of all consecutive subwords of a word in a triangular grid. Under the folding condition, the boundary between length ascents and descents must contain a folding square. Its equal opposite vertices identify two letters that can be deleted. Induction proves the deletion condition for involutory generators.

Words: 31

If w=s1​⋯sn​ is a reduced expression and s is simple with ℓ(ws)<ℓ(w), then
ws=s1​⋯sj​​⋯sn​
(14)
for some index j. The analogous statement holds for multiplication on the left.
Matsumoto theorem

Matsumoto's theorem says that any two reduced expressions for one element of a Coxeter group are connected by a finite sequence of braid moves.
Tits word reduction theorem

Every word in simple Coxeter generators can be reduced by braid moves and cancellations ss↦1. Consequently, a word is reduced exactly when no sequence of braid moves can make a cancellation possible.

σ(xi​)v=v−⟨v,ei​⟩ei​.

(σ∗(w)f)(v)=f(σ(w−1)v).

The Coxeter complex has faces represented by cosets wWJ​ of standard parabolic subgroups, ordered by reverse inclusion. Geometrically, its maximal simplices are the chambers of the Coxeter arrangement intersected with a sphere.

The wall associated with a reflection r consists of the Cayley-graph edges fixed setwise and reversed by left multiplication by r. Its complement has two connected components.

The two connected components of the complement of a wall of a Coxeter group are its half-spaces. A wall separates two group elements when they lie in opposite half-spaces.

A subset T⊆S is spherical when its standard parabolic subgroup WT​ is finite.

The Davis complex is the geometric realization of the poset of cosets wWT​ for spherical subsets T⊆S. Equivalently, it is the basic construction of a Coxeter group obtained by gluing copies of the Davis chamber along mirrors. It is a contractible proper W-CW complex.

U(W,K)=(W×K)/∼,

For involutory generators, the folding condition requires that simple multiplication never preserve length and that simultaneous left and right ascents either combine to a two-step ascent or fold: if both si​w and wsj​ have length ℓ(w)+1, then either ℓ(si​wsj​)=ℓ(w)+2 or w=si​wsj​.

For generators si​,sj​ with mij​<∞, the braid relation equates the two alternating words of length mij​ beginning with si​ and sj​, respectively. When mij​=2, it says that the generators commute.

The E7​ Coxeter graph is the simply-laced seven-vertex tree whose three arms have lengths 1, 2, and 3. Its Coxeter Gram matrix is positive definite and has determinant 2.

A BN-pair in a group G consists of subgroups B,N such that G=⟨B,N⟩, H=B∩N is normal in N, and W=N/H has distinguished involutory generators satisfying the Bruhat multiplication axioms. The quotient W is its Weyl group.

A Hecke algebra is a deformation of the group algebra of a Coxeter group, obtained by deforming the quadratic relations for its simple generators while retaining the braid relations.

qi​=[B:B∩x˙i​Bx˙i−1​].

In characteristic zero, a finite-dimensional Lie algebra is a semidirect sum of its solvable radical and a semisimple Lie subalgebra. The group analogue splits appropriate groups as a semidirect product with a Levi subgroup.
